article_title: Development of an interactive tutorial on quantum key distribution
citation: Seth DeVore and Chandralekha Singh. (2014). Development of an Interactive Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. 2014 PERC Proceedings. https://doi.org/10.1119/perc.2014.pr.011
title: Quantum Interactive Learning Tutorial (QuILT) on quantum key distribution
description: A research-based tutorial that helps upper-level undergraduates learn quantum mechanics through quantum key distribution with a simple two state system. It 'uses a guided approach in which various concepts build upon each other gradually', covering the B92 protocol with non-orthogonal photon polarization states and a second protocol using entangled spin-1/2 particles, with prediction phases, a checking simulation, and a table students must construct.
requirements: Students first work through basics: the article states 'The QuILT first helps students learn the basics related to bits, qubits, polarization states of a photon, and effect of measurement on a two state system in a superposition of linearly independent states.'
constraints: Part II using entangled particles 'was given to students as homework after traditional instruction on relevant concepts including two state systems' such as spin-1/2 and photon polarization states.
target_learners: upper-level undergraduate students enrolled in quantum mechanics courses
target_learning_goals: effect of quantum measurement collapsing a state into an eigenstate
detecting an eavesdropper in secure QKD protocols
examples: Students must construct a table spanning 'all possible combinations of Alice's polarization, Bob's polarization, whether or not Bob's detector clicks and whether a bit is generated' (Table 1).
key_sources: Seth DeVore and Chandralekha Singh. (2014). Development of an Interactive Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. 2014 PERC Proceedings. https://doi.org/10.1119/perc.2014.pr.011

article_title: Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution
citation: DeVore, S. and Singh, C. (2013). An Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=An+Interactive+Learning+Tutorial+on+Quantum+Key+Distribution
title: Predict-then-reconcile guided inquiry sequence within the tutorial
description: The QKD QuILT organizes its guided inquiry around a predict-check-reconcile cycle: students first predict what should happen in a given situation, then receive a figure and table from which the correct outcome can be inferred, and are then asked to reconcile any difference between their prediction and the provided information before proceeding. The article states that "The QKD QuILT asks students to predict what should happen in a particular situation and after their prediction phase is complete, they are provided a figure and table from which they can infer what they should have predicted." This cycle appears in the warm-up basics, the insecure orthogonal-polarization protocol, and the secure non-orthogonal protocol, culminating in students completing Table 1 across all combinations of Alice's and Bob's polarizations and detector clicks.
requirements: Guiding questions sequenced so concepts build on each other gradually
Figures and tables provided after the prediction phase against which students check their predictions
constraints: Designed for use in small groups in class or as homework after traditional lecture instruction on the relevant basics
target_learning_goals: connecting the formalism and conceptual aspects of quantum mechanics in the context of quantum key distribution
examples: Students complete Table 1 predicting whether a bit is recorded and which bit, then compare with Figure 2 showing the probabilities that a bit is recorded in each case
key_sources: DeVore, S. and Singh, C. (2013). An Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=An+Interactive+Learning+Tutorial+on+Quantum+Key+Distribution

article_title: Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution
citation: DeVore, S. and Singh, C. (2013). An Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=An+Interactive+Learning+Tutorial+on+Quantum+Key+Distribution
title: Quantum Interactive Learning Tutorial (QuILT) on quantum key distribution with non-orthogonal photon polarization states
description: The QKD QuILT is a research-validated instructional tutorial on quantum key distribution using single photons with two non-orthogonal polarization states, comprising a warm-up on bits, qubits, photon polarization and measurement, an insecure orthogonal-polarization protocol, and the secure non-orthogonal protocol including eavesdropper analysis. The article states it "actively engages students in the learning process and helps them build links between the formalism and the conceptual aspects of quantum physics without compromising the technical content." Students work through it in small groups of 2-3 in class, typically spending around 1.5 hours total including in-class time, with unfinished portions completed as homework.
requirements: Traditional lecture instruction on photon polarization states and a basic outline of QKD before students begin the tutorial
A pretest after traditional instruction and a posttest after tutorial completion
constraints: Guides students through an ideal situation in the absence of decoherence; the effect of decoherence is discussed but neglected over small distances
target_learners: upper-level undergraduate physics majors, typically juniors and seniors
target_learning_goals: understanding how secure QKD protocols exploit measurement disturbance and the no-cloning property to detect eavesdropping
examples: Administered in class to all students in the 2009, 2010, and 2013 offerings of the first-semester upper-level quantum mechanics course at a large research university
key_sources: DeVore, S. and Singh, C. (2013). An Interactive Learning Tutorial on Quantum Key Distribution. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=An+Interactive+Learning+Tutorial+on+Quantum+Key+Distribution
